name: pr_open_draft
description:
Open one draft pull request on Ledgerline's repository that proposes, in prose, the change for one issue. The branch is always repomind/issue-<number>; the remote needs no commits, and nothing checks the proposed change. Open it before the triage comment and only when the triage names a file: an issue whose file is none gets no pull request. A draft PR can be closed later, unlike a comment. Opening it again in the same run writes nothing new and returns the first PR.

Returns JSON: {"pr": "pr-7", "issue": "issue-4417", "branch": "repomind/issue-4417", "state": "open", "draft": true, "replayed": false}; "replayed": true means this PR was already open, and nothing new was written. There is no empty result: a success always names the PR. The title is limited to at most 120 characters and the body to at most 4,000; a longer one, an empty one, a branch other than repomind/issue-<number>, or an issue that does not exist is an error and opens nothing.

number.description: The issue's number, as a bare integer: 4417 for issue-4417. The PR is linked to this issue.

branch.description: Exactly repomind/issue-<number>, with the same number: repomind/issue-4417 for issue 4417. Any other branch is refused, so that a repeat of this call finds the PR it already opened.

title.description: One line, 1 to 120 characters, saying what the change fixes or adds, e.g. "Await the backoff delay in withRetry". Shown in the PR list.

body.description: 1 to 4,000 characters of Markdown. Name the file the triage chose, relative to the repository root, on its own line as "file: <path>", then propose the change in prose: what is wrong, where, and what to change. No code diff is needed.

input.title: Await the backoff delay in withRetry
input.body:
file: src/util/retry.ts

withRetry computes backoffDelay before each retry but never awaits it, so all attempts fire at once. Await the delay before the next attempt.

examples.note: The typical call: the branch built from the issue number, the file on its own line, the change in prose.

input.title: Document the export endpoint's date range parameters
input.body:
file: docs/API.md

The Export section does not say which date range parameters the endpoint accepts or in which time zone. Add them to that section, with one example request.

examples.note: A hard case: a docs issue, whose file is a document, still gets a PR. The branch keeps the exact form repomind/issue-<number>; never a descriptive branch name such as fix/export-docs.
